title: conservative-shelf-profiles-warmstart-and-unit-econ-metrics
author: Elena M. Ortiz
body: Motivation: aggressive quant/batch defaults can produce cost wins but sometimes cause regressions for tail-latency or prompt-sensitive workloads. This PR introduces a conservative "shelving" concept (shelf profiles) plus warmstart/warmup templates and a minimal unit-economics metric export so ops can safely adopt cost presets with observability. Summary of changes: 1) new shelf profile schema (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with explicit gating flags to opt-in to quantization/compact kernels; 2) warmstart templates that run a short sequence of safe-prefill steps when a model shard is cold, reducing cold-start token overhead and smoothing SLO regressions; 3) unit-econ export under /metrics/econ with per-route per-model cost breakdown (tokens, GPU-time-ms, cache-hit-rate); 4) CLI: rw-econ apply-shelf and rw-econ simulate to preview econ impact; 5) docs and migration guide. Checklist: - [x] Add shelf schema and runtime enforcement - [x] Implement warmstart templates and scheduler hook - [x] Expose unit-econ metrics and Prometheus labels - [x] Provide CLI simulation and YAML examples - [x] Add docs + upgrade notes - [x] E2E smoke tests in canary cluster Release impact: non-breaking default; conservative profile is the default to avoid regression risk. Ops can opt into balanced/aggressive profiles per-route or per-tenant. Related: ENG-7843 for shelf design, ENG-8019 for unit-econ metric format. Testing: local unit tests (econ package), e2e smoke run on canary, synthetic load profiles showing 8-12% token cost reduction on balanced and 18-24% on aggressive for batch-friendly workloads while conservative preserves baseline latency. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable conservative shelf by default in Hosted canary for 72h, collect econ metrics, then ramp clients and expose profile chooser in Console. Risks and mitigations: aggressive profile can degrade tail-latency on small prompts; mitigated by conservative default, automatic fallback when cache-hit-rate < 0.3, and rollback via per-route policy. Follow-ups: telemetry to detect if warmstart runs are failing; automated Linear tasks to track customer opt-ins.
commits: feat(econ): add shelf profile schema and runtime gating
feat(runtime): warmstart scheduler hook and prefill templates
feat(cli): rw-econ simulate and apply-shelf commands
docs: econ shelves migration guide and examples
test(econ): add shelf profile unit tests
review_comments: Marcus Li: Looks good overall, but please add a short-circuit to the warmstart path when KV cache warming is disabled by tenant policy.
Author response (Elena): Added short-circuit in shelf_validator.go and unit tests to cover the disabled-cache case.
Priya Raman: CI flaked on the canary e2e run — please split the long-running canary into a separate e2e job or mark as flaky for main CI.
Author response (Elena): Split canary job into e2e_canary in our GitHub Actions matrix and marked it optional; main CI now runs fast smoke. See .github/workflows/e2e.yml change.
Dmitri Volkov: Suggest adding a Prometheus label econ_profile to make dashboarding easier.
Author response (Elena): Added econ_profile and route_id labels to exporter and dashboard example in docs.
release_notes: Add conservative shelf profiles and warmstart templates; introduce unit-econ metrics at /metrics/econ; new rw-econ CLI to simulate and apply shelf profiles. Conservative profile is the default to avoid latency regressions.
